findings.reason: src/constructFrom/index.ts:53 now evaluates `constructFromSymbol in date` whenever typeof date === "object", and that throws for null. normalizeDates/index.ts:27 picks a null argument through `typeof date === "object"`, so the throw reaches multi-date functions too. I lowered C1 from high to medium: the DateArg types exclude null, so only untyped JS callers hit this, and toDate/index.ts:60 already throws on null in the same way.
findings.claim: Removing the `date &&` guard makes constructFrom(null, value) throw a TypeError instead of returning new Date(value), and this also affects normalizeDates when one of its arguments is null.
findings.evidence: The diff changes `if (date && typeof date === "object" && constructFromSymbol in date)` to `if (typeof date === "object" && constructFromSymbol in date)`. When `date` is null, `typeof date === "object"` is true, so the next step evaluates `constructFromSymbol in null`, which throws. Callers that can pass a null date at runtime include `src/constructNow/index.ts:36` (`return constructFrom(date, Date.now())`) and `src/_lib/normalizeDates/index.ts:25-27` (`constructFrom.bind(null, dates.find((date) => typeof date === "object"))`). In normalizeDates, `find` picks a null argument because typeof null is "object", so every multi-date function that goes through normalizeDates now throws when any of its date arguments is null, where it used to return a Date.
